answer: Each identity locks a 100-credit margin bond for one island tide position; the island board publishes the tide delta each epoch, and a position below the delta threshold is liquidated, burning its bond. Positions are key-isolated, so losses cannot offset gains elsewhere: the k-th fake needs its own 100 margin plus a 20 fee, and 1,000 fakes lock 100,000 and pay 20,000, with no netting. A cross-margin netting ring fails because the board recomputes each position against the published delta separately. An honest agent holds one position, keeps margin, and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
